traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria and technical requirements of docs/stories/010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT.story.md are implemented and verified: - Core Functionality & Format (REQ-SUPPORTS-PARSE, REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION): valid-annotation-format + valid-implements-utils parse `@supports story-path REQ-ID...`, enforce presence of story path and ≥1 requirement, and validate both story path and IDs against patterns. Tests under "[REQ-IMPLEMENTS-PARSE]" and multiple "[REQ-FORMAT-VALIDATION]" cases confirm correct behavior and error handling. - Validation & Requirement Scoping (REQ-SUPPORTS-VALIDATE, REQ-SCOPED-IDS, REQ-ERROR-CONTEXT): valid-req-reference and its helpers resolve the story file for each @supports line, load that story’s requirement IDs, and report `reqMissing` with both reqId and storyPath. Multi-story fixtures in tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts show the same REQ ID reused across different story files and validated per-story, with explicit messages including the checked story path. - Rule Integration & Backward Compatibility (REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-SUPPORTS, REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT, REQ-MIXED-SUPPORT): require-story-annotation and require-req-annotation treat @supports as satisfying their respective requirements while still enforcing legacy @story/@req semantics. Mixed usage in the same comment/function is explicitly tested in valid-annotation-format, and numerous legacy-only tests remain green, confirming no regression. - Mixed Usage at Codebase Level: Tests demonstrate functions/comments that mix @story, @req, and @supports in one block, and that both styles are valid throughout the codebase. No tests require exclusive use of a single style, aligning with mixed-usage acceptance criteria. - Quality Standards: Implementation follows established ESLint rule patterns (helpers, schema validation, clear messages, exhaustive tests) and is covered by a comprehensive Jest suite that all passes in the current run. - Documentation: README and rule documentation references (via rule names and descriptions) explain @supports, its role in test traceability, and the migration from legacy annotations. This satisfies the documentation acceptance criterion and reflects the ADR’s decision to standardize on @supports. Given that the story content matches the previously assessed version, the relevant implementation files are present, and all tied tests pass in the latest full test run, this story is fully implemented and remains in a passing state.
